rv.q: Let’s Play Highly Recommends The Last Pair of Earlies At The Raven Theatre.
If you are drawn to powerful story-telling, this is a top pick for your time.

Allen’s newest work is a loving (if somewhat tempered) testament to the Black pioneers who reshaped Chicago, and a bittersweet portrait of lovers who set out to change themselves—and at the peril of their marriage, succeed.
This world premiere by Chicago playwright Joshua Allen that opens Raven’s new season, sensitively shaped and guided by the extremely talented Wardell Julius Clark, was well worth the wait.
Joshua Allen’s bittersweet fable of dreams deferred through erosive attrition, rather than overt opposition, is more inclined to find its counterparts in historical fact.
The actors and creative team are to be commended for their talent.

cn.t: Joshua Allen's world premiere about dreams deferred earns warm praise for its sensitive storytelling and precisely choreographed dual-timeline staging, marking a promising return to live theater at Raven.
